title: Fail-closed pre-push review with round budgets
summary: The pre-push review stops being advisory. `--warn-only` is removed, so `osf review run` now fails a push on a kept must-fix or should-fix finding, and on a review that could not run. To keep that from looping forever, a per-worktree round counter lives in the journal state (outside the worktree the builder can edit) and lets the push through after `in_sandbox_rounds` failed rounds, while a separate `could_not_run_rounds` budget ends a could-not-run streak with a named block instead of a silent pass. A credential preflight decides a missing key or login file before any reviewer process starts, login-file secrets are now scrubbed from output, the work item can arrive through `OSF_WORK_ITEM`, and the pull-request workflow no longer re-runs on a body edit.

nodes.label: moon review task
nodes.subtitle: osf review run --if-enabled
nodes.summary: The pre-push task. It loses `--warn-only`, gains `--work-item .osf/out/work-item.txt`, and its inputs now include the work item file and `$OSF_WORK_ITEM` so a changed work item cannot reuse a cached review.

nodes.label: .osf/out/work-item.txt
nodes.subtitle: or OSF_WORK_ITEM
nodes.summary: The work item body the caller writes before the push. When the file is missing, `OSF_WORK_ITEM` supplies the same text.

nodes.label: review run
nodes.subtitle: review_run_exit_code
nodes.summary: Runs every enabled reviewer, then hands the outcome to `finish_review` with round counting on. The `--warn-only` flag is gone from the argument struct.

nodes.label: finish_review
nodes.subtitle: verdict + kept findings → exit code
nodes.summary: Computes the base exit code from the verdict and whether any kept finding is must-fix or should-fix, then, when counting rounds, asks the round budget whether the push may proceed.

nodes.label: round_kind / review_base
nodes.subtitle: Pass | Findings | CouldNotRun
nodes.summary: Classifies a finished round. A could-not-run verdict spends the could-not-run budget even when another lens kept a finding; a pass with a blocking finding spends the findings budget.

nodes.label: round_allows_push
nodes.subtitle: the pre-push budget
nodes.summary: A pass clears the counts. A findings round increments and lets the push through once past the limit. A could-not-run round increments and, past its own limit, returns an error naming the block rather than a pass.

nodes.label: RoundCounts
nodes.subtitle: load / save / clear
nodes.summary: The serialized counter, keyed by the canonical worktree path so each develop run has its own count.

nodes.label: ReviewConfig
nodes.subtitle: in_sandbox_rounds, could_not_run_rounds
nodes.summary: Two new round limits, both defaulting to 3 and both refused when zero. The whole-run timeout default drops from 2700 to 1800 seconds.

nodes.label: osf.toml [review]
nodes.subtitle: concurrency 16, 1800s
nodes.summary: The repository's own review settings, sized for thirteen lenses and two reviewers inside the whole-run limit. The opencode secret is renamed to OSF_REVIEW_OPENCODE_API_KEY.

nodes.label: preflight_and_not_run
nodes.subtitle: missing_credentials
nodes.summary: Decides before any worker starts whether a reviewer has no way to sign in. A reviewer already skipped for a more specific reason, or with no read-only mode, is not judged again.

nodes.label: Reviewer::missing_credentials
nodes.subtitle: credential env + login paths
nodes.summary: A credential variable counts when non-empty; a login file counts when any of its paths exists under the real home. A templated reviewer is never judged, since its template may carry its own auth.

nodes.label: secret_values::held
nodes.subtitle: login-file leaves
nodes.summary: Now also collects every string leaf of the agents' JSON login files, so a provider key kept in opencode's auth file is scrubbed from output like an environment token.

nodes.label: read_work_item
nodes.subtitle: file, then OSF_WORK_ITEM
nodes.summary: Falls back to `OSF_WORK_ITEM` when no path is given or the path is not found; any other read error stays an error. Text from the environment is always the body, never the saved-JSON form.

nodes.label: changeset_risk::changed_files
nodes.subtitle: filters .osf/
nodes.summary: Untracked files under `.osf/` are dropped from the change, so osf's own round counter or SARIF output cannot change which lenses the next round selects.

nodes.label: review reduce
nodes.subtitle: never counts rounds
nodes.summary: The pull-request reduce step shares `finish_review` but passes `count_rounds = false`, so a kept should-fix fails every time and never becomes a budget pass.

nodes.label: journal state dir
nodes.subtitle: review-rounds/<sha>.json
nodes.summary: The state directory outside the worktree. The round count file is named by the sha of the canonical worktree path.

nodes.label: review.yml
nodes.subtitle: pull_request_target
nodes.summary: The base-branch workflow. It no longer triggers on `edited`, so a body edit does not start another review.

nodes.label: review-check.yml
nodes.subtitle: build, review, reduce
nodes.summary: The reusable workflow that holds every job and remains the merge authority.

edges.label: --work-item, no --warn-only
edges.summary: The pre-push task now calls the review without the flag that forced exit 0, so the review's own exit code gates the push.

edges.label: count_rounds = true
edges.summary: The run path counts rounds; the reduce path does not.
The verdict and the blocking flag become a base exit code and a round kind.

edges.label: kind, limits
edges.summary: The budget decides whether a failing round actually stops the push.
Loads, increments and saves the counter for the round's kind.

edges.label: review-rounds/*.json
edges.summary: The counter is read and written under the journal state, never in the worktree.

edges.label: in_sandbox_rounds, could_not_run_rounds
edges.summary: The limits come from the trusted config root's `[review]` section.
The repository's own review settings load through the same parser.
Each reviewer is judged before its worker starts.
The preflight asks the reviewer whether it has any way to sign in.
The work item text is read from the file or the environment before any lens runs.

edges.label: body text
edges.summary: The caller writes the body before the push; the environment is the fallback.
Lens selection reads the change, which no longer includes osf's own untracked output.
Reviewer output is scrubbed against environment tokens and login-file leaves.

edges.label: count_rounds = false
edges.summary: The pull-request path shares the verdict rule but never spends the pre-push budget.
The caller workflow still delegates every job to the reusable one.

flows.title: A pre-push review round and its budget
flows.summary: One `osf review run` at pre-push: the work item is resolved, reviewers are preflighted, the review runs, and the round budget decides whether the push stops.

messages.label: read body
messages.note: The file is tried first; a missing file falls back to OSF_WORK_ITEM.

messages.label: credential check
messages.note: A reviewer with no key and no login file is recorded could-not-run and starts no worker.

messages.label: save counts
messages.note: A pass removes the file; a failed round increments its own counter.

messages.label: may push?
messages.note: Past the could-not-run limit the answer is an error naming the block, never a pass.

messages.label: exit 0 / 1 / 2
messages.note: The exit code now gates the push; there is no --warn-only to force zero.
